item.title: Automorphisms and Hodge isometries of surfaces with $K^2=p_g=1$
item.description: arXiv:2610.33364v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $S$ be a minimal complex surface of general type with $K_S^2=p_g(S)=1$. By a theorem of Catanese, the canonical model of $S$ is a complete intersection of two sextics in $\mathbf{P}(1,2,2,3,3)$ whose equations admit a normal form, and the global Torelli theorem fails for these surfaces. We describe $\operatorname{Aut}(S)$ in terms of the coefficients of the normal form, prove that $|\operatorname{Aut}(S)|\leq 72$, and classify the surfaces attaining the bound: two surfaces with singular canonical model and a one-parameter family $X_r$ of smooth surfaces. For the surfaces $X_r$ we compute a basis of the primitive cohomology consisting of eigenvectors of a subgroup $\mathbf{Z}/6\mathbf{Z} \times \mathbf{Z}/6\mathbf{Z}$ of $\operatorname{Aut}(X_r)$, given by residues of explicit polynomials, together with the intersection form in this basis. We then show that the natural map from $\operatorname{Aut}(X_r)$ to the group of Hodge isometries of the primitive lattice modulo $\pm1$ is injective but has image of index at least $331\,776$, so that the Torelli principle for automorphisms fails for these surfaces.
item.dc:creator: Jorge Duque Franco, Alvaro Liendo, Pedro Montero

item.title: GKZ Systems and Gauss-Manin Connections of Families of Projective Hypersurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.33602v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Periods of projective hypersurfaces satisfy GKZ hypergeometric systems, which may have solutions that do not arise as periods. For deformations of Fermat hypersurfaces, we describe the Gauss-Manin connection in terms of images of contiguity operators between GKZ systems. These images are also realized as Fourier transforms of minimal extensions of Kummer modules.
item.dc:creator: Ryo Negishi

item.title: Movable Curves and Ample Normal Bundles
item.description: arXiv:2610.33724v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the movable cone of a smooth complex projective variety is the closed cone generated by possibly singular curves with ample coherent normal sheaves, answering a question of Boucksom--Demailly--P\u{a}un--Peternell. For smooth curves, we establish the analogous equality in several geometric settings and give explicit constructions on blowups.
item.dc:creator: Jingcao Wu

item.title: Brauer--Manin obstruction for Weil restrictions
item.description: arXiv:2610.33736v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a quasi-projective variety $X$ defined over a number field $k$, let $X'$ be its Weil restriction with respect to a finite field extension $k/k'$. We prove that the Brauer--Manin set of $X$ agrees with the Brauer--Manin set of $X'$. We also prove the agreement for Brauer--Manin set of them given by $\mathrm{Br}_1$.
item.dc:creator: Hui Zhang

item.title: Uniform asymptotics and the Weil--Petersson constant
item.description: arXiv:2610.33752v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In their celebrated work on the large-genus asymptotic expansion of Weil--Petersson volumes, Mirzakhani and Zograf left open the question of whether the Weil--Petersson constant satisfies $C_{\mathrm{WP}}=\pi^{-1/2}$. We resolve the conjecture affirmatively. Our strategy is to consider a family of spectral curves interpolating between $y=z-4z^3$ and $y=\sin(2\pi z)/(2\pi)$. For each fixed number $n\geq2$ of marked points, we normalize the cusp coefficients using the action integral and the derivative at its first positive zero. We prove that the logarithmic derivatives of these normalized coefficients with respect to the family parameter are $O_n(g^{-1})$, uniformly along the family. The proof combines the descendant recursion, positivity, the dilaton equation, KdV, and coefficient asymptotics for the Painlev\'e I equation.
item.dc:creator: Kefeng Liu, Hao Xu

item.title: Explicit equations of three pairs of fake projective planes
item.description: arXiv:2610.33823v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We find explicit polynomial equations in their bicanonical embeddings into $\mathbb C\mathbb P^9$ for the pairs of fake projective planes labeled by $(C18,p=3,\{2\},D_3), (C18,p=3,\{2\},(dD)_3)$ and $(C18,p=3,\{2\},(d^2D)_3)$ in the Cartwright-Steger classification. We do this by starting with the equations of the commensurable fake projective plane labeled by $(C18,p=3,\{2I\})$ that were found in arXiv:2512.03213.
item.dc:creator: Lev Borisov, Nathan Mann

item.title: Global invertibility of polynomial mappings and connectedness of preimages of large spheres
item.description: arXiv:2610.33875v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that a polynomial mapping $\mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^2$ with nowhere zero Jacobian determinant is a global diffeomorphism provided the preimage of large circles are connected. In higher dimensions this result fails and we present families of counterexamples. Yet, in dimension $3$, we prove that if the preimages of large spheres are connected, then the Jelonek set of the mapping is not homeomorphic to a line and, provided that it has codimension at least $2$, cannot have a single end at infinity.
item.dc:creator: Francisco Braun, Zbigniew Jelonek, Maria Michalska

item.title: The generalized Dixmier conjecture and the two-dimensional Jacobian conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.33919v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the two-dimensional Jacobian conjecture $\mathrm{JC}_2$ implies the generalized Dixmier conjecture $\mathrm{DC}'_1$ for the first Weyl algebra $A_1$, which states, in one of several equivalent formulations, that every endomorphism of the two-by-two matrix ring $\operatorname{Mat}_2(A_1)$ is invertible. For the converse, an endomorphism of $\mathbb A^2_{\mathbb C}$ with Jacobian one gives rise to a family of holonomic $A_2$-modules over finite fields. One needs to lift this family to an $A_2$-module in characteristic zero with the prescribed arithmetic support. The existence of such a lift is a special case of Kontsevich's conjecture on holonomic $\mathcal D$-modules with prescribed arithmetic support. We prove that in this special situation such a lift is unique whenever it exists. If these lifts exists for every endomorphism with Jacobian one, then $\mathrm{DC}'_1$ implies $\mathrm{JC}_2$. For every $n\ge 3$, we construct a Lagrangian subvariety of $T^*\mathbb{A}^n$ that provides a counterexample to Kontsevich's conjecture. The counterexamples arise from the graph of a noninvertible symplectic endomorphism of $\mathbb A^4$ constructed by Long. We also present a different strategy for lifting $\mathcal D$-modules associated with a Jacobian-one endomorphism of $\mathbb A^2_{\mathbb C}$ to characteristic zero via ultraproducts and show that the existence of a characteristic-zero lift in this setting is equivalent to the uniform boundedness of the Berest--Wilson invariants of these $A_2$-modules, regarded as left $A_1$-modules. Finally, we study two other conjectures of Kontsevich on arithmetic support, giving a counterexample to one and partial results on the other.
item.dc:creator: Alexey Kanel-Belov, Timofey Fedorov

item.title: Delta Characters and Ranks of Minimal Subisocrystals of Abelian Schemes
item.description: arXiv:2610.33948v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using the framework of delta characters on arithmetic jet spaces, we construct a canonical sequence of filtered isocrystals associated to an abelian scheme $A$ of relative dimension $g$ over a $p$-adically complete discrete valuation ring. These isocrystals map injectively via a canonical morphism into the first (rational) crystalline cohomology group $\mathbf{H}^1_{\mathrm{cris}}(A)$ of the abelian scheme $A$, directly generalizing a prior construction due to Borger and Saha. Pandit showed that the canonical morphism is a map of isocrystals. This then implies that the image of this canonical embedding coincides with the minimal subisocrystal $F_{\mathrm{cris}}(\Omega_A)$ containing the space of invariant differential forms $H^0(A,\Omega_A)$. Berthelot and Ogus showed that the dimension of $F_{\mathrm{cris}}(\Omega_A)$ is $g$ if and only if $A$ has an endomorphism that lifts the absolute Frobenius on the special fiber of $A$. As a primary application, for a general abelian scheme $A$, we show that the minimal subisocrystal $F_{\mathrm{cris}}(\Omega_A)$ can be viewed as a module obtained from primitive delta characters of $A$ via appropriate twists by the canonical Frobenius morphism $\phi$ induced from the theory of arithmetic jet spaces. As a consequence, we show that the rank of $F_{\mathrm{cris}}(\Omega_A)$ depends on numerical invariants arising from the theory of delta characters of $A$. More precisely, the dimension of $F_{\mathrm{cris}}(\Omega_A)$ is given by the sum of the exact orders of the primitive delta characters associated to the abelian scheme $A$.
item.dc:creator: Rajat Kumar Mishra, Arnab Saha

item.title: Hodge--Deligne polynomials and $S_n$-representations on the cohomology of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.33971v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compute the Hodge-Deligne polynomials of the moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n}$ of stable $n$-pointed curves of genus two, together with the action of the symmetric group $S_n$ on their cohomology, for all $n$. Using Hassett's moduli spaces of weighted pointed curves, we first show that the generating function of the $S_n$-equivariant Hodge-Deligne polynomials of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}$ is obtained from that of the moduli spaces of minimally weighted pointed curves by plethysm with the explicit symmetric function $Z=h_1-\sum_{k\ge3}(x+x^2+\dots+x^{k-2})h_k$; numerically, this is an explicit change of variables. The latter spaces map to $\overline{\mathcal M}_g$, and over each boundary stratum they are built from punctured universal curves and Losev-Manin spaces. Combining the stratification by stable graphs with Burnside's formula and twisted characteristics, we obtain in genus two a closed formula whose only non-elementary input is the cohomology of symplectic local systems on $\mathcal M_{1,1}$ and $\mathscr A_2$, known by work of Eichler-Shimura and Petersen. This determines the $S_n$-representations on all $H^{p,q}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n})$ for $n\le 19$ and on all even degree $H^{p,q}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n})$ for every $n$. We carry out the computation in all degrees for $n\le 18$, where it agrees with an independent computation by point counts, and in even degrees for $n\le 30$. As an application, we find that the even degree cohomology of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n}$ is of Hodge-Tate type if and only if $n\le 20$: the space $H^{23,1}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,21})$ is the multiplicity free $S_{21}$-representation with Frobenius characteristic $s_1\cdot h_2[e_{10}]$, of dimension $1939938$, so that $H^{24}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,21})$ is not spanned by algebraic cycle classes.
item.dc:creator: Young-Hoon Kiem

item.title: Fine points of the moduli space of cubic rational maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.33990v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A rational point of the moduli space $\mathcal{M}_3$ of cubic rational maps is fine if its conjugacy class contains a map defined over $\mathbb{Q}$, and coarse otherwise. In the invariants $\xi_0,\dots,\xi_5$ that embed $\mathcal{M}_3$ in $\mathbb{P}(2,2,3,3,4,6)$, we prove that a point with trivial automorphism group is fine if and only if the quaternion algebra $(-m_{12},-2\xi_0)_{\mathbb{Q}}$ splits, where $m_{12}=\frac{1}{3}\xi_0^2\xi_1+\xi_0\xi_4-\xi_3^2$; we give the analogous criterion on the locus $\mathcal{L}_2$ of maps with an involution and show that all other strata are fine. The proof is constructive and yields an explicit descent. We prove that the obstruction class is unramified along every divisor of the compactification, that a prime $p\ge 5$ obstructs only if the point reduces modulo $p$ into the closure of one of the two codimension-two loci $\mathcal{L}_1$, $\mathcal{L}_2$ of maps with an involution, and that $\mathcal{M}_3$ has transverse $A_1$-singularities along both, above which the class ramifies; local densities predict that $\mathcal{L}_2$ is met modulo $p$ with probability $\asymp 1/p$, so that it carries the obstruction. A census of all 214,260,288 rational points of weighted moduli height at most 7 agrees with this mechanism and supports the conjecture that the proportion of fine points tends to zero like $(\log B)^{-1/2}$.
item.dc:creator: Tanush Shaska

item.title: On the Torsion Subgroup of the N\'eron--Severi Group
item.description: arXiv:2610.34115v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove an explicit bound for the torsion subgroup of the N\'eron--Severi group of a smooth projective complex variety. The proof combines the Diophantine-approximation method of Ziyang Gao and the author (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.22285) with Lefschetz fibrations. As an application, we deduce an explicit bound for the torsion sections of a traceless abelian scheme over a complex curve.
item.dc:creator: Kaiyuan Gu

item.title: Recovering the Topology of a Real Plane Algebraic Curve by Tropical Homotopy
item.description: arXiv:2610.34392v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a tropical homotopy method for computing the numbers of ovals and unbounded components of a real plane algebraic curve, together with the pairing of its ends at infinity. Under explicit support and nondegeneracy assumptions, the homotopy starts from a tropical patchwork and encounters finitely many events. At Morse event points, the curve changes by local surgery. To determine the global attachments, we follow descending separatrices of a single gradient-like field to a fixed collection of base curves. The order of their landing points defines a finite combinatorial state, updated by local rules that also handle events at infinity and simultaneous event points. This recovers component data without tracing the intervening curves. For the dequantizing lifting, given by the negative logarithms of coefficient magnitudes, we prove an explicit event window when the lifting is generic. For fixed support and coefficient signs, with independent, identically distributed log-normal magnitudes, the expected number of events is bounded by a constant divided by the standard deviation of the logarithms. When all event points are Morse, correctness is conditional on complete, correctly classified event data, a sufficiently small starting parameter, and correctly labelled and ordered landing points. A numerical implementation illustrates its behaviour on sparse curves of high degree and on coefficients spanning many scales; these conditions are not certified.
item.dc:creator: Weixun Deng

item.title: Indeterminacy of period map and Griffiths heights for hypersurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.34429v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the period map $\overline {\mathcal P}$, from the GIT moduli space of degree $d$ hypersurface $X$ in $\mathbb P^n$ to the Baily-Borel compactification of the period image associated to the middle cohomology $H^{n-1}_{\rm prim}(X,\mathbb Z)$, extends regularly to $X$ if and only if $X$ has at worst nodal singularities (resp. suspensions of slc surface singularities) when $n$ is even (resp. $n$ is odd). This verifies and generalizes Laza-O'Grady's prediction on the indeterminacy locus of the period map for quartic K3s to arbitrary hypersurfaces. For Calabi-Yau hypersurfaces, we prove that the birational map from the GIT moduli space to the BBH compactification extends regularly to $X$ if and only if $X$ has semi-log canonical singularities. The results apply to distinguish the Baily-Borel and BBH compactifications. In the process, we answer two questions of Mordant on the Griffiths height for families of hypersurfaces over curves, which are crucial to the proofs of the main results.
item.dc:creator: Sung Gi Park

item.title: Spectra, Growth, and Localization in Half-Bounded Tensor Triangular Geometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.34469v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Over a noetherian scheme, classical cohomological support determines thick tensor ideals of perfect complexes. In half-bounded derived categories, complexes with the same support can generate different radical thick tensor ideals. We study how these distinctions affect the Balmer spectrum and localization. For a commutative noetherian ring $R$, we prove that $\operatorname{Spc}(\mathbf D^-_{\mathrm{fg}}(R))$ is noetherian if and only if $R$ is artinian. For a nonempty noetherian scheme $X$, the corresponding condition is $\dim X=0$. For such a ring $R$ and a finite group $G$, $\operatorname{Spc}(\mathbf D^-_{\mathrm{fg}}(RG))$ is noetherian if and only if $R$ is artinian and $|G|$ is invertible in $R$. Using the Sanders--Zhang classification over a discrete valuation ring, we compare objects whose annihilator exponents grow at different rates in different degrees. We lift the relevant generation relations before changing coefficients and obtain spectral retractions. These comparisons persist after thick quotients and algebraic localization under explicit uniform annihilation and nonvanishing conditions. A second argument uses nonnilpotent classes of positive degree and passes from cyclic subgroups to finite groups. Applications include relative results for schemes and bounded-below spectra with degreewise finitely generated homotopy. We also describe the cohomological information shared by the resulting ideals. The localization comparisons for bounded-below complexes of finitely generated modules and for bounded-below derived objects with finitely generated cohomology are established separately.
item.dc:creator: Liangyu Zhu

item.title: Correlation inequalities for volume polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.34562v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish sharp correlation inequalities for volume polynomials associated with covers of multisets. These inequalities simultaneously generalize the Khovanskii--Teissier and reverse Khovanskii--Teissier inequalities for intersections of nef divisor classes on projective varieties. They also hold for volume polynomials arising from convex bodies and Hermitian matrices, recovering and extending classical results such as the Alexandrov--Fenchel inequality for mixed volumes of convex bodies and the Hadamard--Fischer inequality for determinants of positive semidefinite matrices. As a combinatorial application, we prove a negative correlation inequality for partitions of bases of matroids that are linearly realizable over a field.
item.dc:creator: June Huh, Mateusz Micha{\l}ek, Botong Wang, Jian Xiao

item.title: Hodge Theory and Grobner Degenerations
item.description: arXiv:2610.34641v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the behavior of mixed Hodge structures under square-free Grobner degenerations. We show that the weight-zero part of singular cohomology and the zeroth graded piece of the Hodge filtration are preserved under such degenerations, complementing the homological rigidity established in the seminal work of Conca and Varbaro. We use these results to settle their conjecture concerning the singularities of homogeneous coordinate rings admitting such degenerations.
item.dc:creator: Ritvik Ramkumar

item.title: Sheaves on nodal singularities I
item.description: arXiv:2610.34676v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study two families of moduli spaces of sheaves attached to the node, namely the punctual Hilbert schemes of the non-reduced plane curve $x^uy^v=0$, and the punctual Quot schemes of the module $k[[x]]^u\oplus k[[y]]^v$ over the reduced node $xy=0$. We compute their motivic generating functions for all $u,v$ and over every field. Both are specializations of a single rational function whose numerator counts matrices by rank, and they are related by the substitution $\mathbb{L}\mapsto Q\mathbb{L}$. This proves the Hilb--Quot correspondence for the node with independent ranks on the two branches. The main geometric ingredient is an elementary modification of an ideal along a branch of the curve, whose fibres are affine spaces of dimension equal to a contact length. We also construct stratifications of the Hilbert schemes into products of affine spaces and tori, and we formulate a branchwise Hilb--Quot--HOMFLY conjecture, which we test on the colored Hopf link.
item.dc:creator: Yifeng Huang, Ruofan Jiang, Alexei Oblomkov

item.title: Elementary transformations of toric vector bundles
item.description: arXiv:2610.34885v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We describe negative and positive elementary transformations of toric vector bundles in terms of Klyachko filtrations. We first determine the filtrations of the restriction of a toric vector bundle to an invariant prime divisor and then derive explicit formulas for the transformed bundle: only the filtration at the distinguished ray changes. As applications, we interpret adding and removing invariant boundary components of logarithmic tangent bundles as elementary transformations and recover the residue sequence for logarithmic cotangent bundles.
item.dc:creator: Sukmoon Huh

item.title: Voevodsky's motives and zeroth slice of motivic sphere
item.description: arXiv:2610.34898v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $S$ be a noetherian scheme of finite Krull dimension and let $R$ be a commutative ring in which every positive residue characteristic of $S$ is invertible. We prove that Voevodsky's stable Nisnevich category of motives with $R$-coefficients is canonically equivalent to modules over the zeroth slice of the motivic sphere with derived $R$-coefficients. The comparison identifies the corresponding commutative coefficient algebras and is compatible with arbitrary pullback. The theorem applies to singular and nonreduced schemes, including mixed-characteristic bases, and requires no excellence or finite-type hypothesis. Its special cases include rational coefficients over arbitrary bases, arbitrary coefficients over $\mathbb Q$-schemes, and $\mathbb Z[1/p]$-algebra coefficients over $\mathbb Z_{(p)}$-schemes. The proof establishes base change for finite-cycle spectra using permutation quotients, families of cycles, and arithmetic power homotopies, then passes to general bases by universal homeomorphism invariance and continuity.
item.dc:creator: Bo Zhang

item.title: Sharp effective Nullstellensatz for projective Cohen-Macaulay schemes
item.description: arXiv:2610.34946v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we prove a sharp effective Nullstellensatz for projective Cohen-Macaulay schemes of pure dimension over an arbitrary field. In particular, if L is an ample line bundle on a smooth complex projective variety X and J is a coherent ideal sheaf with J\otimes L globally generated, then (\sqrt{J})^{\deg_L X}\subseteq J. This establishes the sharp bound conjectured by Ein and Lazarsfeld. More generally, we obtain sharp bounds in terms of mixed intersection numbers and a refinement involving products of powers of prime ideal sheaves associated to the irreducible components of the base locus. We also establish sharp radical power bounds for homogeneous ideals in finitely generated standard graded Cohen-Macaulay domains, extending Koll\'ar's sharp effective Nullstellensatz for polynomial rings. The proofs combine purity and cycle preservation for leading Ext sheaves with Koszul evaluation maps compatible with successive divisor cuts.
item.dc:creator: Zhi Li, Xiankui Meng, Xiaoyu Su, Langfeng Zhu

item.title: On irregular threefolds of Kodaira dimension two
item.description: arXiv:2610.34955v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $X$ be an irregular threefold of Kodaira dimension two. We show that the Iitaka volume $\operatorname{Ivol}(X)$ of $X$ is at least $\frac{1}{100}$ and $\lvert mK_X\rvert$ defines the Iitaka fibration for $m\geq 32$. Both $\frac{1}{100}$ and $32$ are sharp.
item.dc:creator: Ziqi Liu, Pengjin Wang

item.title: Automorphisms of $\mathbb{P}^1$-bundles over rational surfaces in positive characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2610.35024v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study $\mathbb{P}^1$-bundles over smooth projective rational surfaces over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$, together with the actions of their neutral automorphism groups. After an equivariant square birational reduction to the projective plane or a Hirzebruch surface, we classify the possible induced actions on the base and identify the families relevant to relative maximality. For $p\geq 3$, we prove that every such $\mathbb{P}^1$-bundle is equivariantly square birational to one whose neutral automorphism group is relatively maximal, and we classify all bundles with this property. We also describe all equivariant square birational maps between these relatively maximal bundles and determine which are stiff or superstiff, the analogues of rigidity and superrigidity for $\mathbb{P}^1$-bundles.
item.dc:creator: J\'er\'emy Blanc, Ronan Terpereau

item.title: Quasi locally free sheaves on primitive double schemes
item.description: arXiv:2610.35033v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $X_2$ be a complex primitive double scheme, $X=(X_2)_{red}$. The ideal sheaf of $X$ is a line bundle on $X$. Let $E$ be a coherent sheaf on $X_2$. Then there exists a nonempty open subset $U$ of $X_2$ and integers $m_1$, $m_2$, uniquely determined by $E$, such that $E_{|U}$ is locally isomorphic to $(O_X\otimes C^{m_1})\oplus(O_{X_2}\otimes C^{m_2})$. If we can take $U=X_2$, we say the $E$ is quasi locally free. If $m_1=1$ we say that $E$ is rigid. In this case, we show that deformations of $E$ are of the same type. So locally free sheaves and rigid quasi locally free sheaves on $X_2$ play the same role on $X_2$ as locally free sheaves do on smooth schemes. In this paper we study the existence and description of quasi locally free sheaves, and flat families of such sheaves.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Marc Dr\'ezet

item.title: Mustafin degenerations of six points in the projective plane and self-duality
item.description: arXiv:2610.35060v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mustafin varieties provide a framework for degenerating the projective plane together with marked points, governed by the combinatorics of Bruhat-Tits buildings. Such limit objects are parametrized by the boundary points of a projective compactification of the moduli space of $n$ points in $\mathbb{P}^2$ constructed by Schaffler-Tevelev. In this paper, we study the locus of this compactification generically parametrizing self-dual configurations, or equivalently, six points lying on a conic. We prove that this locus is a tropical compactification of the moduli space of self-dual configurations, with associated fan a refinement of the self-dual tropical Grassmannian introduced by Geiger-Hashimoto-Sturmfels-Vlad. We show that this compactification is a blow up of $\overline{\mathrm{M}}_{0,6}$ and we classify the objects it parametrizes: degenerations of $\mathbb{P}^2$ equipped with a stable $6$-pointed rational curve that records the limiting conic.
item.dc:creator: Alheydis Geiger, Luca Schaffler

item.title: Finiteness of algebraic Weil-Petersson totally geodesic curves in pointed moduli spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.35086v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every pair $(g,n)$ with $2g-2+n>0$, we prove that $\mathcal M_{g,n}$ contains only finitely many closed algebraic curves that are totally geodesic for the Weil-Petersson metric. We show that every such curve is an arithmetic quadratic Teichm\"uller curve and has equal heights for all marked maximal cylinders in every periodic direction. Although there are infinitely many arithmetic Teichm\"uller curves, we can bound the degree of the associated torus covering by the crucial equal-height property. This leads to the desired finiteness statement. We also prove that quadratic Teichm\"uller curves are characterized by the existence of a holomorphic splitting of the logarithmic cotangent Kodaira-Spencer map. This result is the analogue of M\"oller and Viehweg's characterization of Kobayashi geodesics in $\mathcal A_g$.
item.dc:creator: Tianzhi Hu, Kang Zuo

item.title: Number of equations defining the Kummer varieties of hyperelliptic curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.35097v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Jacobian of an hyperelliptic curve $C$ of genus $g$ over $\mathbb{C}$ is equipped with a symmetric theta divisor $\Theta$ that defines a principal polarization. The line bundle $\mathcal{O}(2\Theta)$ defines an embedding of the Kummer variety $K$ inside the projective space $\mathbb{P}^{2^g-1}$, which factorizes inside a certain orthogonal Grassmannian. We describe a minimal free resolution of $K$ inside this Grassmannian using geometric representation theory. As a consequence, we obtain a formula for the number of quartic equations defining $K$ in the projective space $\mathbb{P}^{2^g-1}$.
item.dc:creator: Nathan Partouche

item.title: Universal polynomials for Gromov-Witten invariants on toric surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.35122v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the polynomiality of combined logarithmic and ordinary Gromov-Witten invariants with a Lambda class insertion on toric surfaces $\Delta(\mathbf{c},\mathbf{d})$. We show that the combined logarithmic Gromov-Witten invariants can be expressed in terms of universal relative node polynomials when the direction vector $\mathbf{c}$ and length vector $\mathbf{d}$ of the $h$-transverse lattice polygon $\Delta(\mathbf{c},\mathbf{d})$ are sufficiently large and spread out. In particular, when the normal fan of the $h$-transverse lattice polygon $\Delta(\mathbf{c},\mathbf{d})$ is smooth and its edges satisfy a length condition, we show that the combined Gromov-Witten invariants are equal to a universal node polynomial. We also show that the higher genus Block-G\"ottsche polynomials of smooth toric surfaces corresponding to these $h$-transverse lattice polygons, including toric blowups beyond Hirzebruch and toric del Pezzo surfaces, are equal to a generating function of higher genus Gromov-Witten invariants.
item.dc:creator: Yanqiao Ding, Dadi Ni

item.title: Deformations of the logarithmic tangent bundle of smooth projective surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.35127v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study fixed-determinant deformations of the logarithmic tangent bundle associated with a smooth irreducible divisor on a smooth complex projective surface. We derive numerical criteria for the existence of positive-dimensional deformation families. Using the Enriques--Kodaira classification and Miyaoka-type inequalities, we classify the minimal surface pairs whose logarithmic tangent bundle is infinitesimally rigid. We also prove monotonicity under compatible blow-ups and compute local comparison formulas for resolutions of low-multiplicity ordinary singularities of the boundary.
item.dc:creator: Sukmoon Huh, Min-Gyo Jeong

item.title: Uniqueness of the maximal function field with the third largest genus in characteristic $3$
item.description: arXiv:2610.35241v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $n$ be a positive integer and define $q=3^n$. It is well known that there exists a maximal function field $Z_3$ over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$ of genus $g_3=q(q-1)/6$ and that $g_3$ is the third largest genus a maximal function field over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$ can have. In this article we show that any maximal function field over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$ of genus $g_3$ is isomorphic to $Z_3$. This extends previously known uniqueness result for the largest and second largest genera of maximal curves.
item.dc:creator: Peter Beelen, Maria Montanucci, Jonathan Niemann

item.title: The Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequence can be arbitrarily non-degenerate in positive characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2610.35243v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: There is a long tradition of constructing smooth projective varieties in positive characteristic with non-degenerate Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequences. In this paper, we show that for any $n\geq 1$ and any spot $(i, j)$ on the $E_n$-page, except for the cases where the differential is forced to be zero for trivial reasons, there exists a smooth projective variety whose Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequence has a non-zero differential with source $E_n^{i, j}$. Our construction is inspired by constructions of nilmanifolds in complex geometry and can be regarded as a positive characteristic analogue.
item.dc:creator: Kehao Cheng

item.title: Solvability and nilpotence of ind-groups via tangent curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.35418v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Answering a question of Kraft and the second-named author, we prove that a connected ind-group over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero is solvable, respectively nilpotent, if and only if its Lie algebra is. Their derived lengths, respectively nilpotency classes, coincide. We also obtain bounds on the derived length and nilpotency class for regular linear representations of connected ind-groups and for subgroups generated by connected algebraic subgroups. As an application, we give a new proof of the geometric case of a theorem of Belabbas: a solvable Lie algebra of vector fields on an affine variety generated by finitely many locally finite Lie subalgebras is locally finite and finite dimensional.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Perepechko, Mikhail Zaidenberg

item.title: Symplectic singularity as hyperK\"ahler cone
item.description: arXiv:2610.35510v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that any symplectic singularity has a structure of hyperK\"ahler cone. In particular, it is equivalent to the vertex of a conical symplectic variety, and it is automatically K-polystable.
item.dc:creator: Yuji Odaka

item.title: Positivity of Relative Pluricanonical Direct Images via Fixed-Point Metrics
item.description: arXiv:2610.35590v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a direct analytic approach to positivity of relative pluricanonical direct images through a fixed-point Hermitian metric by direct differential curvature calculations. The curvature resolvent formula from fixed-point equation leads to two-sided estimates of entire Nakano curvature by determinant curvature. In this way, we identify generic rank of determinant curvature with birational variation dimension for a projective algebraic fibration between smooth connected projective varieties with general fiber of general type and maximal birational variation, assuming $mK_F$ is globally generated or the $m$-canonical map is birational for general fiber $F$. In the global generation case, Green--Griffiths Conjecture asks for the tautological bigness of the ordinary symmetric powers $\operatorname{Sym}^{\ell}f_*\omega_{X/Y}^{\otimes m}$, without passing to reflexive hulls, for $\ell\geq P_m(F)=h^0(F,mK_F)$ whenever $m\geq 1$. We prove it for all $\ell\geq1$ at levels $m\geq 2$, also in the case of birational $m$-canonical map, but construct a counterexample at level $m=1$. Over curves, curvature and boundary estimates give a direct analytic proof of Viehweg's ampleness theorem requested by Fujino. For smooth projective families, we also establish numerical dimension and vanishing results related to the birational variation dimension.
item.dc:creator: Jixiang Fu, Yunyang Xiao

item.title: Maximal curves with trivial automorphism group
item.description: arXiv:2610.35788v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct algebraic curves with trivial geometric automorphism group by taking cyclic scalar quotients of curves of the form \[ y^r-y=xR(x),\qquad r=p^e. \] We give a condition on the genus under which the quotient has no nontrivial automorphism. The proof uses the ramification of a degree-$r$ morphism to the projective line, Castelnuovo--Severi, and explicit automorphisms of the covering curve. The quotient also has gonality $r$, with a unique morphism of degree $r$ to the projective line up to an automorphism of the latter. Applying the construction to maximal additive curves gives explicit maximal curves with trivial geometric automorphism group in every positive characteristic, including families defined over the prime field and of unbounded genus. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first examples of maximal curves with trivial geometric automorphism group. Every maximal curve in these families is covered by the Hermitian curve. For every odd prime $p$ and every $n\ge2$, we prove that the curve $\X_{p,n}$, maximal over $\F_{p^{4n+2}}$, is not a Galois subcover of the corresponding Hermitian curve, even over the algebraic closure. Thus every odd characteristic yields an infinite family of curves covered but not Galois covered by the Hermitian curve. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first such infinite families.
item.dc:creator: Daniele Bartoli, Herivelto Borges, Marco Timpanella, Giovanni Zini

item.title: Characterising canonical lifts of ordinary Calabi-Yau varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.35807v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Brantner-Taelman's canonical lifts of ordinary Calabi-Yau varieties and characterise their (quasi)canonical lifts in terms of rational $p$-adic Hodge theoretic data. We also show that these canonical lifts need not be of CM type and that the associated local Galois representations need not split as sums of twists of unramified representations, in contrast to classical results for abelian varieties and K3 surfaces.
item.dc:creator: Samuel A. Moore

item.title: One ring to rule them all: syzygy maximization for Argyres-Douglas
item.description: arXiv:2610.33151v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose a uniform construction of affine schemes encoding the Higgs branches and Macdonald indices of the Argyres--Douglas theories $\mathcal{D}_p(ADE)$, with $\gcd(p,h^\vee)=1$. The construction captures conjectural OPE decoupling relations via the Jacobian ring of a single invariant polynomial potential, obtained from a polynomial twisted period of the corresponding Coxeter orbit space. We show that these potentials are ``syzygy-maximizing'' in the first jet schemes and recover the Higgs branches as their reduced critical loci. We obtain closed determinant expressions for the classical types and explicit potentials for $E_6$, $E_7$, and $E_8$. Powers of the nilradical define an intrinsic filtration on the resulting Jacobian rings, from which we compute candidate Macdonald indices with the correct Schur and Hall--Littlewood limits, in the examples studied. Restricting the potentials to Slodowy slices extends the prescription to nilpotently Higgsed theories. We further conjecture that these Jacobian rings are isomorphic to Zhu's $C_2$-algebras of simple affine VOAs at boundary admissible levels and their quantum Drinfeld--Sokolov reductions.
item.dc:creator: Monica Jinwoo Kang, Craig Lawrie, Jaewon Song

item.title: Height growth of rational self-maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.33570v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $K$ be a number field or a function field of a curve. Let $f$ be a dominant rational self-map of a normal projective variety $X$ of dimension $d$ over $K$, and let $h_H\geq1$ be an ample Weil height. Let $\lambda_1(f)$ denote the first dynamical degree of $f$. We show that there is a constant $C_{f,h_H}>0$ such that, for any $n\geq1$ and any point $P\in X(\overline{K})$ with well-defined forward orbit, $h_H(f^n(P))\leq C_{f,h_H}h_H(P)n^{2(d-1)}\lambda_1(f)^n$ if $\lambda_1(f)>1$, and $h_H(f^n(P))\leq C_{f,h_H}h_H(P)n^{2d}$ if $\lambda_1(f)=1$. Over number fields, the proof combines a new uniform upper bound for arithmetic degrees with a uniform comparison of point heights. Over function fields, it relies on the corresponding uniform upper bound for geometric degrees on a projective model.
item.dc:creator: Fei Hu, Jiarui Song

item.title: Polynomial Residual Networks are Generically Identifiable
item.description: arXiv:2610.33738v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove identifiability results for constant-width residual networks with polynomial activations and bias terms. For activations of degree at least five with generic coefficients, the fiber over a generic parameter is a singleton. For activations of degree at least three with no linear term after a suitable translation of the input, the generic fiber is given by translating biases and then scaling weights and translated biases by real roots of unity. These results specialize to networks without bias terms. With the same proof technique, we further derive necessary conditions for critical points of the ResNet parametrization, that are central in singular learning theory.
item.dc:creator: Isabel Dahlgren, Giovanni Luca Marchetti, Kathl\'en Kohn

item.title: Ramification in $\mathbf{E}_{n}$-algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.33754v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study $\mathbf{E}_n$-algebras with ramification in their $\pi_0$ and in particular show that the existence of ramification places strong limitations on their chromatic behavior. In particular, we show that $\pi_0$ of nonzero $K(1)$-local $\mathbf{E}_4$-$\mathrm{KU}$-algebras cannot have a map from the ring of integers in a ramified extension of $\mathbf{Q}_p$, and we show that a $p$-complete $\mathbf{E}_2$-ring with a map from a perfectoid ring into its $\pi_0$ is an associative $\mathbf{Z}_p$-algebra.
item.dc:creator: Sanath K. Devalapurkar, Ishan Levy

item.title: Homological and homotopical epimorphisms in monoidal $\infty$-categories
item.description: arXiv:2610.34592v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We compare homological and homotopical epimorphisms of associative algebras in monoidal $\infty$-categories. Assume that geometric realizations and pushouts of associative algebras exist and that tensoring preserves geometric realizations. Then every homological epimorphism is homotopical. If, in addition, the ambient category is additive and tensoring preserves finite coproducts, the converse holds. This extends the result of Chuang and Lazarev for dg-algebras. In the symmetric monoidal setting, we discuss consequences for centers and commutative refinements, as well as applications to derived analytic geometry.
item.dc:creator: Federico Bambozzi

item.title: Hartl's dictionary and a transcendence characterization of equicharacteristic local shtukas with complex multiplication
item.description: arXiv:2610.34822v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We update Hartl's dictionary between $p$-adic Hodge theory and its equicharacteristic analog to include aspects related to the Hodge--Tate filtration in $p$-adic Hodge theory and its equicharacteristic analog, the Hodge--Tate--Taguchi filtration. Using this update, we establish a transcendence characterization of equicharacteristic local shtukas with abelian Tannakian structure group, matching a result of Howe--Klevdal in the $p$-adic setting. A special case of this result says that a formal Drinfeld module over an equicharacteristic local field has complex multiplication if and only if the Hodge--Tate--Taguchi filtration on its $z$-adic Tate module is algebraic.
item.dc:creator: Minhua Cheng, Sean Howe

item.title: Dynamical Chowla conjecture for polynomials of several variables
item.description: arXiv:2610.34912v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In 1965, Chowla conjectured that the mean value of the Liouville function at non-square one-variable polynomials is zero. This conjecture is a generalization of the prime number theorem (PNT). In 2022, Bergelson and Richter established a dynamical generalization of this form of the PNT. For non-square multivariate polynomials, one also expects that Chowla's conjecture is true. In this article, we extend Bergelson and Richter's result to multivariate polynomials whose Birch rank is sufficiently large in terms of their degree. We also establish analogous results for averages over integer points on algebraic varieties.
item.dc:creator: Biao Wang, Daodao Yang

item.title: Faithful Localization of Vertex Algebra Modules
item.description: arXiv:2610.34953v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish a Faithfulness Theorem for vertex algebra modules, showing that two complementary geometric localizations can jointly detect global algebraic structure. We apply this principle to vertex algebras obtained by BRST reduction from classical invariant theory and identify them, under natural geometric hypotheses, with global sections of sheaves of chiral differential operators. As consequences, we prove vanishing of BRST cohomology in nonzero degrees and simplicity, and show that every finitely strongly generated module is a finite direct sum of copies of the vacuum module. In particular, the corresponding module category is equivalent to the category of finite-dimensional vector spaces. For families associated with classical groups, we identify the associated varieties with Hamiltonian reductions, proving quasi-lisse-ness and the predicted identification with Higgs branches of the corresponding supersymmetric gauge theories. This provides geometric realizations of a broad class of vertex algebras arising from three- and four-dimensional quantum field theories.
item.dc:creator: Tomoyuki Arakawa, Xuanzhong Dai, Bailin Song

item.title: Intersection multiplicity of a sparse curve and a trinomial curve
item.description: arXiv:2610.35037v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let f $\in$ C[x, y] be a trinomial and let g $\in$ C[x, y] be a sparse polynomial with N monomials (N $\ge$ 1). We address the problem of bounding the local intersection multiplicity of the bivariate polynomial system f = g = 0 at an isolated root q $\in$ (C * )^ 2 only in terms of N . Our main result establishes that the local multiplicity of the system at any isolated solution q $\in$ (C * ) ^2 is at most (N -1)(N +2)/ 2 , independently of the degrees of f and g. Furthermore, we know that this bound is sharp for N = 3.
item.dc:creator: Jean Mousseau (LAMA)

item.title: Geometry of holonomic modules over the first Weyl algebra
item.description: arXiv:2610.35447v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a geometric description of the formal local data of holonomic modules over the first Weyl algebra, the algebra of differential operators in one variable. The exponential part of the associated formal meromorphic connection is encoded by a truncated jet of an affine plane curve at infinity, and the regular part by a regular formal meromorphic connection. We prove that these geometric data uniquely determine the `elementary' blocks in the formal decomposition of holonomic modules. The resulting correspondence is equivariant under automorphisms of the first Weyl algebra, including the Fourier transform.
item.dc:creator: A. V. Petukhov, M. D. Sulimov

item.title: Uniform large-genus asymptotics of Weil-Petersson volumes
item.description: arXiv:2610.35492v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $V_{g,n}$ denote the Weil--Petersson volume of the moduli space of genus-$g$ hyperbolic surfaces with $n$ cusps. We obtain an asymptotic expansion in inverse powers of the genus as $g\to\infty$, uniformly for all $n\ge0$. This includes cusp counts of order $\sqrt g$ and larger, where the fixed-$n$ expansion of Mirzakhani and Zograf no longer gives a uniform approximation. The leading term is explicit and has relative error $O(g^{-1})$. Truncating the expansion at a suitably chosen order proportional to $\sqrt g$ gives relative error $O(\exp(-a\sqrt g))$ for some $a>0$, with no restriction on the growth of $n$. For fixed $n$, the leading term identifies the universal constant in the Mirzakhani--Zograf asymptotics as $1/\sqrt\pi$, as conjectured by Zograf. We also answer two questions of Mirzakhani: we determine explicit asymptotic profiles for volume ratios uniformly in the number of cusps, and for adjacent coefficient ratios of the one-boundary volume polynomial uniformly over all degrees. The proof uses a positive recursion for mixed $\kappa_1$--$\psi$ intersection numbers, with the absolute normalization determined by comparison with the known asymptotics of pure $\psi$ intersection numbers.
item.dc:creator: Zhiyi Li, Qihang Wang

item.title: How to get an attractive model
item.description: arXiv:2610.35798v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a fourth-order Calabi-Yau differential operator, which seems to have been missed by earlier tabulations. We draw attention to this operator because of its clear geometric interpretation and evidence that it possesses a rank-two attractor, conjecturally giving a new example of a Calabi-Yau threefold with modularity properties analogous to those of an elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$.
item.dc:creator: Joseph McGovern

item.title: Which Schubert varieties are local complete intersections?
item.description: arXiv:1111.6146v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We characterize by pattern avoidance the Schubert varieties for GL_n which are local complete intersections (lci). For those Schubert varieties which are local complete intersections, we give an explicit minimal set of equations cutting out their neighborhoods at the identity. Although the statement of our characterization only requires ordinary pattern avoidance, showing that the Schubert varieties not satisfying our conditions are not lci appears to require more general notions of pattern avoidance. The Schubert varieties defined by inclusions, originally introduced by Gasharov and Reiner, turn out to be an important subclass, and we further develop some of their combinatorics. Applications include formulas for Kostant polynomials and presentations of cohomology rings for lci Schubert varieties.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society 107 (2013) 1004-1052
item.dc:creator: Henning \'Ulfarsson, Alexander Woo

item.title: Isogenous components of Jacobian surfaces
item.description: arXiv:1902.06372v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathcal{X}$ be a genus 2 curve defined over a field $K$, $\mathrm{char}\, K = p \geq 0$, and $\mathrm{Jac}(\mathcal{X}, \iota)$ its Jacobian, where $\iota$ is the principal polarization of $\mathrm{Jac}(\mathcal{X})$ attached to $\mathcal{X}$. Assume that $\mathrm{Jac}(\mathcal{X})$ is geometrically $(n,n)$-reducible with $E_1$ and $E_2$ its elliptic components. When $K$ is a number field, we count such curves up to geometric isomorphism, among those admitting a model over $K$. For $n=2$ and $\mathrm{Aut}(\mathcal{X}) \cong V_4$ we prove that, for each $N=2,3,5,7$, there are infinitely many curves $\mathcal{X}$ for which $E_1$ and $E_2$ are $N$-isogenous. For $n=2$ and $\mathrm{Aut}(\mathcal{X}) \cong D_4$ the elliptic quotients from the two classes of nonhyperelliptic involutions are always $2$-isogenous, and for each $N=3,5,7$ only finitely many curves have them $N$-isogenous. For $n=3$ there are infinitely many curves with $N$-isogenous elliptic components for each $N=2,3,5$, while for $N=7$ there are only finitely many such curves with a model over $\mathbb{Q}$. Furthermore, we determine the Kummer and the Shioda-Inose surfaces for the above $\mathrm{Jac}(\mathcal{X})$ and show how such results in positive characteristic $p>2$ suggest nice applications in cryptography.
item.dc:creator: Lubjana Beshaj, Artur Elezi, Tony Shaska

item.title: On Base Change of Local Stability in Positive Characteristics
item.description: arXiv:2001.04083v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $X\to(C,c)$ be a flat family over a smooth curve germ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$, with geometrically integral generic fiber. We show that the fiber pair stays log canonical after every finite dominant base change by a smooth curve if and only if it is log canonical after every finite Frobenius base change, including the original stage. More specifically, under iterated Frobenius pullback, a negative log discrepancy of a vertical divisor goes to minus infinity. For any fixed separable cover, however, log canonicity along the Frobenius tower of the original family gives a uniform lower bound instead. Putting these two bounds side by side gives the result for separable covers of arbitrary degree. We also illustrate that the single first Frobenius base change does not suffice in our criterion by an example. Finally, we include two more examples related to the main problem. Neither resolution of singularities nor inversion of adjunction is used.
item.dc:creator: Zhi Hu, Runhong Zong

item.title: Moduli Spaces of Homologically Trivial Parabolic (Higgs) Bundles on the Projective Line and an Application to the Deligne-Simpson Problem
item.description: arXiv:2101.01913v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish an isomorphism between the moduli space of homologically trivial parabolic (Higgs) bundles on $\mathbb{P}^1$ and the quiver variety associated to a star-shaped quiver. As an application, we give a Hitchin-theoretic construction of irreducible solutions to the nilpotent additive Deligne-Simpson problem under explicit numerical assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Xueqing Wen

item.title: One-cycles on Gushel-Mukai fourfolds and the Beauville-Voisin filtration
item.description: arXiv:2202.09811v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the invariant locus of the involution associated to a general double EPW sextic is a constant surface and introduce a filtration on $\CH_1$ of a Gushel-Mukai fourfold. We verify the sheaf/cycle correspondence for sheaves supported on low degree rational curves, parallel to the cubic fourfolds case.
item.dc:creator: Ruxuan Zhang

item.title: Kodaira-type Vanishings via Non-abelian Hodge Theory
item.description: arXiv:2207.09064v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we use nonabelian Hodge theory to study Kodaira-type vanishings. In particular, we generalize Saito vanishing using mixed twistor $\sD$-modules. We also generalize it to a Kawamata-Viehweg type vanishing using $\Q$-divisors, and prove an effective global generation theorem, as an application. We also prove a relative vanishing for a projective morphism in the mixed twistor $\sD$-module setting.
item.dc:creator: Chuanhao Wei

item.title: On the weight zero compactly supported cohomology of $\mathcal{H}_{g, n}$
item.description: arXiv:2307.01819v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For $g\ge 2$ and $n\ge 0$, let $\mathcal{H}_{g,n}\subset \mathcal{M}_{g,n}$ denote the complex moduli stack of $n$-marked smooth hyperelliptic curves of genus $g$. A normal crossings compactification of this space is provided by the theory of pointed admissible $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-covers. We explicitly determine the resulting dual complex, and we use this to define a graph complex which computes the weight zero compactly supported cohomology of $\mathcal{H}_{g, n}$. Using this graph complex, we give a sum-over-graphs formula for the $S_n$-equivariant weight zero compactly supported Euler characteristic of $\mathcal{H}_{g, n}$. This formula allows for the computer-aided calculation, for each $g\le 7$, of the generating function $\mathsf{h}_g$ for these equivariant Euler characteristics for all $n$. More generally, we determine the dual complex of the boundary in any moduli space of pointed admissible $G$-covers of genus zero curves, when $G$ is a cyclic group of prime order, as a symmetric $\Delta$-complex. We use these complexes to generalize our formula for $\mathsf{h}_g$ to moduli spaces of $n$-pointed smooth prime cyclic covers of genus zero curves. This version contains corrections to the published version: see the attached erratum.
item.dc:creator: Madeline Brandt, Melody Chan, Siddarth Kannan

item.title: The Lichtenbaum-Quillen dimension of complex varieties
item.description: arXiv:2312.06930v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Lichtenbaum-Quillen conjecture for smooth complex varieties states that algebraic and topological K-theory with finite coefficients become isomorphic in high degrees. We define the "Lichtenbaum-Quillen dimension" of a variety in terms of the point where this happens, show that it is surprisingly computable, and analyze many examples. It gives an obstruction to rationality, but one that turns out to be weaker than unramified cohomology and some related birational invariants defined by Colliot-Th\'el\`ene and Voisin using Bloch-Ogus theory. Because it is compatible with semi-orthogonal decompositions, however, it allows us to prove some new cases of the integral Hodge conjecture using homological projective duality, and to compute the higher algebraic K-theory of the Kuznetsov components of the derived categories of some Fano varieties.
item.dc:creator: Nicolas Addington, Elden Elmanto

item.title: The fundamental theorem of tropical differential algebra for formal Puiseux series
item.description: arXiv:2312.10036v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The fundamental theorem of tropical differential algebra has been established for formal power series solutions of systems of algebraic differential equations. It has been shown that the direct extension to formal Puiseux series solutions fails. In this paper, we overcome this issue by transforming the given differential system and such a generalization is presented. Moreover, we explain why such transformations do not work for generalizing the fundamental theorem to transseries solutions, and show that one inclusion still holds for this case even without using any transformation.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Falkensteiner, Stefano Mereta

item.title: Les squelettes accessibles d'un espace de Berkovich
item.description: arXiv:2409.08755v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We define a class of skeletons on Berkovich analytic spaces, which we call "accessible", which contains the standard skeleton of the n-dimensional torus for every n and is preserved by G-glueing, by taking the inverse image along a morphism of relative dimension zero, and by taking the direct image along a morphism whose restriction to the involved skeleton is topologically proper.
item.dc:creator: Antoine Ducros, Amaury Thuillier

item.title: The many faces of a logarithmic scheme
item.description: arXiv:2412.12078v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A standard assumption in the study of logarithmic structures is "fineness", but this assumption is not preserved by intersections, fiber products, and more general limits. We explain how a coherent logarithmic scheme $X$ has a natural decomposition into "fine faces" -- a collection of fine logarithmic subschemes. This allows for importation of the techniques of tropical geometry into the study of more general logarithmic schemes. We explain the relevance of the construction in enumerative geometry and moduli via a range of examples. Techniques developed in the study of binomial schemes lead to effective algorithms for computing the fine faces.
item.dc:creator: Thibault Poiret, Dhruv Ranganathan

item.title: Asymptotic coefficients of Weil-Petersson volumes in the large genus
item.description: arXiv:2501.06421v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Mirzakhani-Zograf proved the large genus asymptotic expansions of Weil-Petersson volumes and showed that the asymptotic coefficients are polynomials in $\mathbb Q[\pi^{-2},\pi^2]$. They also conjectured that these are actually polynomials in $\mathbb Q[\pi^{-2}]$. In this paper, we prove Mirzakhani-Zograf's conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Xuanyu Huang

item.title: Low Genus Curves on Compact Shimura Surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2502.11582v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate and compare the behaviors of complex curves on two major types of compact Shimura surfaces: compact variants of Picard and Hilbert modular surfaces. They are quotients of complex hyperbolic balls corresponding to moduli problems for abelian varieties with certain endomorphism types. We prove that if we fix a genus bound, then when the defining discriminant is large enough, low genus curves on the compact variant of Picard modular surfaces do not exist, while low genus curves may persist on the compact variant of Hilbert modular surfaces only if they are special curves, which parametrize those with extra endomorphisms. These results are special cases of a complex function field analogue of uniform boundedness on endomorphism types of abelian varieties. The proof requires understanding the repulsion of special subvarieties and relies on volume estimates in hyperbolic geometry.
item.dc:creator: Zhehao Li

item.title: Quasi-canonical lifting of projective varieties in positive characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2506.01345v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The main aim of this article is to give new classes of smooth projective varieties over characteristic $p>0$ that admit flat liftings over the Witt vectors together with additional data (logarithmic structure and the Frobenius morphism) by showing a descending property of such Frobenius liftability. We establish a refined form of the classical result due to Mehta-Srinivas on the existence of canonical liftings. For this purpose, we also establish a result on the algebraization of certain $p$-adic formal schemes.
item.dc:creator: Ryo Ishizuka, Kazuma Shimomoto

item.title: Descent problem for certificate of non-negativity on semi-algebraic sets
item.description: arXiv:2508.07060v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $F$ be a subfield of $\mathbb R$ and let $K$ be a basic closed semi-algebraic set in $\mathbb R$ with $\partial K\subset F$. Let $\mathcal N$ be the natural choice of generators of $K$. We show that if $f\in F[x]$ is $\geq 0$ on $K$, then $f$ can be written as $$f=\sum_{e\in\{0,1\}^s } a_e\sigma_e g^e $$ where $a_e\in F_{\geq 0}$, $\sigma_e\in \sum F[x]^2$ and $g^{e}=g_1^{e_1} \cdots g_s^{e_s}$. In other words, the preordering $T_{\mathcal N}$ of $F[x]$ is saturated. In case $F=\mathbb R$, this result is due to Kuhlmann and Marshall. As an application, we prove that if $K$ is compact, then $M_{\mathcal N}=T_{\mathcal N}=Pos(K)$. In other words, the quadratic module $M_{\mathcal N}$ of $F[x]$ is saturated.
item.dc:creator: Manoj K. Keshari, Debapriya Ojha, Niladri Sekhar Patra

item.title: Bertini's theorem for $F$-rational $F$-pure singularities
item.description: arXiv:2509.04433v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$, and let $X\subseteq\mathbb{P}^n_k$ be a quasi-projective variety that is $F$-rational and $F$-pure. We prove that if $H \subseteq \mathbb{P}^n_k$ is a general hyperplane, then $X \cap H$ is also $F$-rational and $F$-pure. Of related but independent interest, we present a relationship between the characteristic and index of a $\mathbb{Q}$-Gorenstein variety with isolated non-$F$-regular locus which is $F$-pure but not $F$-regular.
item.dc:creator: Alessandro De Stefani, Thomas Polstra, Austyn Simpson

item.title: Hilbert squares of genus 16 K3 surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2510.26488v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the geometry of a general polarized K3 surface $(S,h)$ of genus 16 and its Fourier-Mukai partner $(S',h')$. We prove that $S^{[2]}$ is isomorphic to the moduli space $M_{S'}(2,h',7)$ of stable sheaves with Mukai vector $(2,h',7)$ and describe the embeddings of the projectivization of the stable vector bundle of Mukai vector $(2,-h',8)$ over $S'$ into these two isomorphic hyper-K\"ahler fourfolds. Following the work of Fr\'ed\'eric Han \cite{Frederic}, we explicitly construct a 3-form $t_1\in \wedge^3 V_{10}^*$, such that $S^{[2]}$ is isomorphic to the Debarre-Voisin fourfold in $G(6,V_{10})$ associated to $t_1\in \wedge^3 V_{10}^*$. Then the reconstruction program is also explained from two perspectives, i.e. in terms of families of stable representations and families of twisted cubics.
item.dc:creator: Junyu Meng

item.title: Failing to keep the balance: explicit formulae and topological recursion for leaky Hurwitz numbers
item.description: arXiv:2603.06094v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recently a new family of enumerative invariants called leaky Hurwitz numbers was introduced by Cavalieri-Markwig-Ranganathan in the context of logarithmic intersection theory. They admit an interpretation via tropical covers where the balancing condition fails. We employ tropical geometry to prove a generalisation of the piecewise polynomiality of Accadia-Karev-Lewanski for leaky completed cycles Hurwitz numbers, and a different wall crossing that is cubic instead of quadratic. Using tropical combinatorics and generatingfunctionology, we also find closed formulae for one-part and two-part completed cycles leaky Hurwitz numbers in genus $0$. Working more generally with a view towards topological recursion, we use Hamiltonian flows to associate spectral curves to very general cut-and-join operators. Under mild analytic constraints, we find the appropriate spectral curves, and in case the leakiness is fixed, we show that the resulting enumerative invariants satisfy topological recursion. This provides a partial inverse to recent work of Alexandrov-Bychkov-Dunin-Barkowski-Kazarian-Shadrin producing differentials satisfying topological recursion for KP $\tau$-functions. In particular these results specialise to completed cycles leaky Hurwitz numbers.
item.dc:creator: Marvin Anas Hahn, Reinier Kramer

item.title: Euclidean distance degree defect of singular projective varieties
item.description: arXiv:2605.13726v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The unit Euclidean distance degree and the generic Euclidean distance degree are two well-studied invariants of projective varieties. These quantities measure the algebraic complexity of nearest-point problems on a variety, and in many examples arising in optimization, engineering, statistics, and data science, there is a significant gap between them. We refer to this difference as the defect of the Euclidean distance (ED) degree. In this paper, we provide a constructible enhancement and a topological formula for the defect of the ED degree of an arbitrary complex projective variety, extending our previous results from the smooth setting. Since the generic Euclidean distance degree is typically more tractable, our approach offers a new method for computing ED degrees in broad generality.
item.dc:creator: Lauren\c{t}iu G. Maxim, Jose Israel Rodriguez, Botong Wang

item.title: Involution-equivariant topological recursion and mirror symmetry for the affine binary dihedral Calabi--Yau threefold
item.description: arXiv:2607.07355v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove a closed-string remodeling statement for the affine binary dihedral Calabi--Yau orbifold threefold $\mathcal X=[\mathbb C^2/\Gamma]\times\mathbb C$, where $\Gamma$ is a binary dihedral subgroup of $SU(2)$. This target lies outside the toric setting of the Bouchard--Klemm--Mari\~{n}o--Pasquetti remodeling conjecture: the toric mirror curve is replaced by the type-$D_l$ relativistic Toda curve of Brini--Ma--Strachan, and the Chekhov--Eynard--Orantin topological recursion is replaced by the $\mathbb Z_2$-equivariant topological recursion of Giacchetto--Kramer--Lewa\'nski, run in the sign sector of the Toda-curve involution with the Prym kernel as its two-point input. We identify the equivariant orbifold quantum cohomology Frobenius manifold of $\mathcal X$ with the invariant Jacobian Frobenius structure of the Toda curve, and we prove that the B-model $R$-matrix, defined by regularized stationary phase, equals the A-side normalized canonical Givental--Teleman $R$-matrix on a chosen simply connected domain; this equality is anchored at the orbifold point through a semistable degeneration of the Toda curve. Comparing the resulting Givental--Teleman and Dunin-Barkowski--Orantin--Shadrin--Spitz graph sums then identifies, after a parity-twisted leaf substitution, the sign-sector recursion with the descendant Gromov--Witten generating functions of $\mathcal X$ in the stable range ($2g-2+n>0$ with $n>0$), and identifies the recursion free energies with the equivariant Gromov--Witten free energies of $\mathcal X$ for $g\geq2$. We also match the genus-one potential defined by the reduced calibrated tau function with the Gromov--Witten potential up to an additive constant.
item.dc:creator: Bohan Fang, Zhuoming Lan, Jingxiang Ma

item.title: Line-filtered ACM bundles and Ulrich defects on abelian varieties of Picard rank one
item.description: arXiv:2608.09163v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $A$ be a complex abelian variety with $\NS(A)=\Z[L]$, $L$ ample. We show that a vector bundle filtered by line bundles splits uniquely into unipotent blocks, determine when it is ACM with respect to $L$, and show that it is never Ulrich. For a rank-two Ulrich bundle we bound from below the degree of the defect of every saturated line subbundle, compute the Hilbert polynomial of the defect, and show that the bound is attained exactly when an explicit cohomological support locus is nonempty. On abelian surfaces this locus is an ample curve in $\Pic^0(A)$; as a consequence, every rank-two Ulrich bundle is a Serre extension of a fixed numerical type, which we characterize and construct for every ample $L$. For $g\ge3$, we reduce the equality case to the existence of subcanonical codimension-two subschemes with prescribed cohomology.
item.dc:creator: Soham Mondal

item.title: Finite Directional Coefficient Modules over Euler Fibers of $A$-Hypergeometric Systems
item.description: arXiv:2609.02449v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let A be a d-by-n integer matrix of rank d, let beta belong to the d-dimensional complex vector space, and consider the A-hypergeometric system defined by the ideal H_A(beta), with relation lattice L equal to the integer kernel of A. No homogeneity, pointedness, or positivity assumption is imposed on A. We study directed formal logarithmic solutions simultaneously over all exponent lattices in the Euler fiber over beta, which form an uncountable family when L has positive rank. For a fixed L-generic direction, negative-support strata are described by rational sign polyhedra, and their directional boundedness is characterized by recession cones. On each exponent lattice, normalization reduces the infinitely indexed coefficient equations to a finite system of Euler, transit, and directional vanishing relations, represented by a finitely presented directional coefficient module. We prove that only finitely many exponent lattices contribute nonzero directed solution spaces and that every contributing coefficient module has finite length. Macaulay inverse-system duality then identifies the dimension of the all-lattice directed formal logarithmic solution space with the length of the all-lattice coefficient module. We also give an explicit formal-series realization and a polynomial colon-ideal criterion for all realizable lowest exponents.
item.dc:creator: Go Okuyama

item.title: Hodge-Deligne and Poincar\'e polynomials of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{1,n}$
item.description: arXiv:2609.12507v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: By studying wall crossings of Hassett moduli spaces of weighted pointed curves, we prove a recursive formula that reduces the computation of the cohomology of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}$ to that of the moduli space $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,(0^+)^n}$ of stable pointed curves of minimal weights. For $g=1$, we further prove an explicit formula for the Hodge-Deligne and Poincar\'e polynomials of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{1,(0^+)^n}$. Combining these, we prove formulas that enable us to compute the cohomology of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{1,n}$ efficiently.
item.dc:creator: Young-Hoon Kiem

item.title: Open extension of a genus zero Hurwitz-Frobenius manifold
item.description: arXiv:2609.26948v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Every Dubrovin--Frobenius manifold provides a solution to the WDVV equation, that was initially formulated in the study of the moduli space of curves. During the last two decades special attention was given to the "open" version of the moduli space of curves. Its genus zero intersection theory is governed by the system of equations called open WDVV equation, that extends "classical" WDVV equation. In this note we study Dubrovin--Frobenius manifold structures on the Hurwitz spaces of genus zero. We construct explicitly the solutions to open WDVV equation for these Dubrovin--Frobenius manifolds and show that these solutions appear as the restriction of the Dubrovin--Frobenius structure to its discriminant.
item.dc:creator: Alexey Basalaev, Anton Rarovskii

item.title: Terracini loci of tangential varieties of Veroneseans
item.description: arXiv:2610.27625v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Terracini locus of a projective variety tells us the sets of points at which Terracini's lemma will fail to recover the dimension of the corresponding secant variety. We study the Terracini loci of tangential varieties of Veronese varieties, classifying several cases, including a complete classification of the Terracini loci of tangential varieties to rational normal curves. We also show that many Terracini loci involve only sets with "intratangent pairs" that lie on the same tangent space to the underlying Veronese variety. Finally, we give some applications to algebraic statistics, showing that osculating varieties of Veronese varieties are moment varieties for local mixtures of location families and connecting Terracini loci to local identifiability.
item.dc:creator: Douglas A. Torrance

item.title: Existence of Ulrich bundles on polarized surfaces and weakly Ulrich bundles on polarized varieties in positive characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2610.28456v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In their seminal paper \cite{eisenbud2003resultants}, Eisenbud and Schreyer asked whether every smooth projective variety admits an Ulrich bundle with respect to each very ample polarization. This question has stimulated extensive research for more than two decades. Recently, Anghel \cite{anghel2026smooth} constructed counterexamples over $\mathbb C$ in dimension two, and Lopez \cite{lopez2026existence} extended this nonexistence result to higher dimensions. In this article, we study the existence problem for sufficiently large multiples of a fixed polarization and derive applications in positive characteristic. Over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic, we prove that every polarized smooth surface admits an Ulrich bundle and every polarized smooth variety admits a weakly Ulrich bundle. Consequently, the Chow forms of surfaces (resp. varieties) admit linear determinantal (resp. determinantal) representations. Moreover, for every such polarized surface, the cone of cohomology tables of coherent sheaves coincides with that on $(\mathbb{P}^2, \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^2}(1))$.
item.dc:creator: Jagadish Pine

item.title: Leafrians, Frobenius splittings, and moduli spaces over Poisson surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.31619v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth projective Poisson surface over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>2$, and let $s\in H^0(X,\omega_X^{-1})$ be nonzero. We construct an anticanonical section associated to $s$, called the leafrian, on moduli spaces $M$ of stable objects on $X$, including the moduli of stable sheaves, of principal $G$-bundles, and of instantons. The leafrian splits $M$ if and only if $s^{p-1}$ Frobenius splits the base. It is invariant under the Hamiltonian flows of Bottacin's Poisson structure on $M$, so every compatibly split subvariety of $M$ is a Poisson subvariety. Furthermore, the leafrian extends to an anticanonical section on the Gieseker compactification $\bar M$, and splits $\bar M$ under the same criterion. As a consequence, for $X$ a rational surface, a ruled surface over an elliptic curve, a $K3$ surface, or an abelian surface, and $\rho>0$, the Gieseker compactification $\bar M$ satisfies Kodaira-type cohomology vanishing, including singular $\bar M$, and the same holds in characteristic zero.
item.dc:creator: Jun Peng

item.title: Handle decompositions and Kirby diagrams for the complement of plane algebraic curves
item.description: arXiv:2306.10519v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The complement of plane algebraic curves are well studied from topological and algebro-geometric viewpoints. In this paper, we will describe the explicit handle decompositions and the Kirby diagrams for the complement of plane algebraic curves. The method is based on the notion of braid monodromy. We refined this technique to obtain handle decompositions and Kirby diagrams.
item.dc:creator: Sakumi Sugawara

item.title: From Cherednik algebras to knot homology via cuspidal D-modules
item.description: arXiv:2407.00971v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove a rational generalization of Haiman's master formula, conjectured by Gorsky and Negu\c{t}: the bigraded Frobenius character of the associated graded of the finite-dimensional representation $L_{m/n}$ of the rational Cherednik algebra at slope $m/n$ can be expressed using the generator of the same slope in the elliptic Hall algebra acting on its polynomial representation. The filtration on $L_{m/n}$ is induced by the Hodge filtration on the cuspidal character $D$-module. As a corollary, we relate the triply-graded Khovanov-Rozansky homology of the torus knot to the sum of hook multiplicity spaces of $L_{m/n}$, proving a conjecture of Gorsky, Oblomkov, Rasmussen and Shende. We further provide a realization of the torus knot homology in terms of explicit coherent sheaves on Hilbert schemes of points in the plane.
item.dc:creator: Xinchun Ma

item.title: On the topological invariance of the algebraic multiplicity of holomorphic foliations
item.description: arXiv:2407.09306v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we address one of the most basic and fundamental problems in the theory of foliations and ODEs, the topological invariance of the algebraic multiplicity of a holomorphic foliation. For instance, we prove an adapted version of A'Campo-L\^e's Theorem for foliations, i.e., the algebraic multiplicity equal to one is a topological invariant in dimension two. This result is further generalized to higher dimensions under mild conditions; as a consequence, we prove that saddle-nodes are topologically invariant. We prove that the algebraic multiplicity is a topological invariant in several classes of foliations that contain, for instance, the generalized curves and the foliations of second type. Additionally, we address a fundamental result by Rosas-Bazan, which states that the existence of a homeomorphism extending through a neighborhood of the exceptional divisor of the first blow-up implies the topological invariance of the algebraic multiplicity. We show that the result holds if the homeomorphism extends locally near a singularity, even if it does not extend over the entire divisor.
item.dc:creator: Leonardo M. C\^amara, Fernando Reis, Jos\'e Edson Sampaio

item.title: Analogues of Traverso's Isogeny Conjecture for Some Unitary p-Divisible Groups
item.description: arXiv:2507.19708v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $p$ be a prime and $\Bbbk$ an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$. Two invariants worthy of study for a $p$-divisible group $X$ over $\Bbbk$ are its isogeny cutoff $b_X$, which measures the amount of $p$-torsion necessary to determine the Newton polygon of $X$, and its minimal height $q_X$, which measures its distance to the closest minimal $p$-divisible group (in the sense of Oort). Traverso's Isogeny Conjecture predicts a bound on $b_X$ in terms of its height and dimension. The conjecture was proved in [NV07] and a refinement was given in [LNV13]; the latter also gives a bound on $q_X$. In this paper, we study these invariants when restricting to the class of supersingular unitary $p$-divisible groups $X$ of signature $(a,g-a)$, where $0 < a < g$, for $p > 2$, and prove further refinements on their bounds purely in terms of $a$.
